UNMET: [fix-code] TEST-1 | WHY: `tests/integration/resume-entry-points-test.sh` explicitly sets `ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0` and uses `runner-state-dir-minimal` (a flat two-leaf template with no cycle), which forces the legacy linear loop. The test's assertion that `intake` emits no `stage.start` on resume therefore exercises the legacy loop's skip guard, not the dispatch-unit loop's. The issue says "A flat fixture such as tests/fixtures/templates/runner-state-dir-minimal.yaml takes the legacy loop, so a test on it passes or fails for the wrong code." All three entry-path sub-cases in that file share this flaw (`ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0` at line 112, 192, 265). | QUOTE: "Tests for R1–R5 must use a cycle. They run a template whose flow has a cycle, so that the runner takes the dispatch-unit loop. A flat fixture such as tests/fixtures/templates/runner-state-dir-minimal.yaml takes the legacy loop, so a test on it passes or fails for the wrong code."
UNSURE: ORDE-1 | WHY: "Do not run this in parallel with another issue that edits the dispatch loop" is an operational/scheduling constraint. Nothing in the diff or repository enforces it mechanically; it cannot be verified by reading the code. What would settle it: CI or issue-tracking evidence that issue #1714 was not in flight concurrently with #1805. | QUOTE: "Do not run this in parallel with another issue that edits the dispatch loop (#1714 touches the allow-list builder in runner.sh)."
UNMET: [fix-design] DISP-1 | WHY: SKIP-1 and LEGC-1 in REQUIREMENTS are both marked "already done" and both cite the same evidence string: `core/pipeline/runner.sh:"When resuming, skip stages already marked complete unless --from-stage overrides"`. That exact text appears at line 3895 of `runner.sh`, inside the legacy linear loop (`for stage in "${active_stages[@]}"`, starting at line 3883), which the issue explicitly names as unreachable for every shipped template. The dispatch-unit loop does have an equivalent guard (lines 3728–3760 for `stage:` units, 3442–3454 for `cycle:` units), so the behavior is correctly implemented — but the requirements were marked "done" on the strength of the legacy loop's text, not the dispatch-unit loop's. | QUOTE: "No requirement may be marked done, and no change made, on the strength of the legacy loop."
